RU-B2-01-001.notes: с- + a multidirectional verb (ходить) makes a perfective meaning a single round trip: схожу = I'll go and come back. It's not 'come down', which is сойти.

RU-B2-01-002.notes: за- + идти means dropping in on the way: зайти к + dative. Зайди ко мне is a casual invitation; к becomes ко before мне.

RU-B2-01-003.notes: раз- + идти + -ся means going off in different directions: разойтись. The reflexive -ся is required, and the past is разошлись.

RU-B2-01-004.notes: пройти is used of time passing: прошло три года. After три the verb is usually neuter singular, as the number phrase isn't treated as a plural subject.

RU-B2-01-005.notes: перейти на «ты» means switching from вы to ты; a common proposal once people get to know each other. перейти also means switching language: перейти на русский.

RU-B2-01-006.notes: съездить is a perfective round trip by transport: went and came back. на выходные gives the planned period, with на + accusative.

RU-B2-01-007.notes: A woman выходит замуж за + accusative (literally 'goes out behind a husband'); a man женится на + prepositional. Mixing them is a classic error.

RU-B2-01-008.notes: пожениться is used only for a couple getting married to each other, so it's always plural. A single person needs выйти замуж or жениться.

RU-B2-01-009.notes: лезть (climb, crawl) is the unidirectional verb; лазить is multidirectional. Its present is irregular: лезу, лезешь, лезет.

RU-B2-01-010.notes: ползти (crawl) is unidirectional; ползать is its multidirectional partner. Its present has stressed endings: ползу, ползёшь, ползёт.

RU-B2-01-011.notes: тащить (drag, haul) is unidirectional; таскать is multidirectional. The stress moves after the я form: тащу́, but та́щит.

RU-B2-01-012.notes: вз- / вос- means upward movement: взойти (rise), past взошло. солнце is neuter, so -ло. The noun восход (sunrise) comes from the same prefix.

RU-B2-01-013.notes: с- + идти means getting off or coming down: сойти с + genitive. It's more bookish than выйти из поезда, which is the usual phrase.

RU-B2-01-014.notes: с- + ехать + -ся means gathering from different places: съехаться. The hard sign ъ separates the prefix from е.

RU-B2-01-015.notes: по- + a multidirectional verb gives a perfective meaning 'for a while': походили по магазинам. The cue tells you the group is mixed, so the plural -ли.

RU-B2-01-016.notes: об- + ездить means covering the whole of an area: объездил всю страну. The ъ separates the prefix об- from е.

RU-B2-02-001.notes: An offer uses the imperfective future: Ты будешь пить чай? The perfective выпьешь would ask whether you'll finish a particular cup.

RU-B2-02-002.notes: Вы будете заказывать? is the waiter's standard question. The imperfective focuses on the activity, which sounds less pushy than закажете.

RU-B2-02-003.notes: Negated perfective futures often mean 'won't be able to': не успею. успеть means managing in time and takes a perfective infinitive.

RU-B2-02-004.notes: не + perfective future expresses impossibility: он не поймёт. The imperfective не будет понимать would describe an ongoing state.

RU-B2-02-005.notes: Without a map you won't find it: не найдёшь expresses impossibility. найти is perfective, irregular: найду, найдёшь.

RU-B2-02-006.notes: пора + imperfective infinitive means 'it's time to': пора идти. The perfective пойти is also heard, but идти is the standard phrase.

RU-B2-02-007.notes: успеть (manage in time) takes the perfective infinitive: успел купить. The focus is on achieving the result before a deadline.

RU-B2-02-008.notes: Не стоит + imperfective means 'there's no point': не стоит волноваться. взволноваться (become agitated) is rare and wouldn't fit.

RU-B2-02-009.notes: удаться (manage, succeed) takes the perfective infinitive: удалось решить. The construction is impersonal, with the person in the dative.

RU-B2-02-010.notes: A warning against something accidental uses не + perfective imperative: не забудь. The imperfective не забывай is a general reminder.

RU-B2-02-011.notes: Не опоздай warns against missing the train by accident; the perfective is used for unintended results. опоздать на + accusative = be late for.

RU-B2-02-012.notes: Осторожно, не упади! is a typical warning: the perfective, because falling is accidental. упасть has the irregular stem упад-.

RU-B2-03-001.notes: удаться is impersonal: мне удалось (I managed). The verb is always third person, and the past is neuter when an infinitive follows.

RU-B2-03-002.notes: прийтись means 'have to' (against one's will): нам пришлось уйти. It's impersonal, with the person in the dative and the neuter past.

RU-B2-03-003.notes: The future of прийтись is придётся: мне придётся работать. It suggests an unwelcome necessity, more than надо.

RU-B2-03-004.notes: стоить + infinitive means 'be worth doing': стоит посмотреть. The infinitive is usually perfective. стоить also means 'cost'.

RU-B2-03-005.notes: следовать + dative + infinitive means 'should' in formal style: вам следует обратиться. It's typical of official advice.

RU-B2-04-001.notes: The participle declines with its noun: о прочитанной книге (prepositional feminine). -анный is the ending for -ать verbs.

RU-B2-04-002.notes: The past active participle agrees with гостями in the instrumental plural: приехавшими. It's formed with -вш-.

RU-B2-04-003.notes: A participle phrase can come before the noun: от работающего в Москве друга. The genitive -его agrees with друга.

RU-B2-04-004.notes: Будучи (being) is the verbal adverb of быть, followed by the instrumental: будучи студентом. It's typical of written style.

RU-B2-04-005.notes: Будучи + instrumental gives a cause: being a doctor, she knew. In speech, one says Так как она врач.

RU-B2-04-006.notes: A process in progress uses the -ся passive of an imperfective (решается); a completed result uses the short perfective participle (решён).

RU-B2-04-007.notes: The agent of a passive goes into the instrumental without a preposition: построен архитектором. English uses 'by'.

RU-B2-05-001.notes: благодаря + dative gives a positive cause: благодаря тебе. It's formed from the verbal adverb of благодарить (thank).

RU-B2-05-002.notes: из-за + genitive gives a negative cause: из-за пробок. Using благодаря here would sound sarcastic. The noun пробка (traffic jam, cork) has the genitive plural пробок.

RU-B2-05-003.notes: в течение + genitive means 'over the course of': в течение недели. The preposition ends in -е, unlike the noun phrase в течении реки (in the river's current).
RU-B2-05-003.tip: в течение (time) ends in -е; в течении реки (river's current) in -и.

RU-B2-05-004.notes: в связи с + instrumental means 'in connection with, due to': в связи с ремонтом. It's a typical phrase on official notices.

RU-B2-05-005.notes: по сравнению с + instrumental means 'compared with'. It's neutral, used in speech and writing. The shorter form в сравнении с is more bookish.

RU-B2-05-006.notes: в отличие от + genitive means 'unlike': в отличие от брата. The two things contrasted must be comparable.

RU-B2-05-007.notes: в зависимости от + genitive means 'depending on'. It comes from зависеть от, which takes the same case.

RU-B2-05-008.notes: при + prepositional means 'in the time of' a ruler: при Петре Первом. Петр has a fleeting ё: Пётр → Петра.

RU-B2-05-009.notes: при + prepositional means 'in someone's presence': при детях. It's also used for 'attached to': при университете.

RU-B2-05-010.notes: из-под + genitive means 'from under': из-под кровати. It combines из (out of) and под (under). The opposite movement uses под + accusative: залез под кровать.

RU-B2-05-011.notes: из-за + genitive also means 'from behind': из-за угла. Context separates it from 'because of'. It pairs with за + accusative for motion behind something: зайти за угол.

RU-B2-05-012.notes: сквозь + accusative means 'through' something that partly blocks: сквозь туман. через is the general 'through, across'.

RU-B2-05-013.notes: зато means 'but on the other hand' and introduces a compensating advantage. It follows a comma and is often preceded by но.

RU-B2-05-014.notes: тем не менее (nevertheless) is set off by commas in the middle of a sentence. It's more formal than всё равно.

RU-B2-05-015.notes: однако (however) can join clauses like но or stand at the start of a sentence. As a conjunction it doesn't need a comma after it.

RU-B2-05-016.notes: при этом means 'at the same time, and yet': it adds a second fact that might seem incompatible with the first.

RU-B2-05-017.notes: то…, то… describes alternating states: то дождь, то снег. Each то starts one of the alternating items.

RU-B2-05-018.notes: не то…, не то… expresses uncertainty between two options: не то в шутку, не то всерьёз. It's more colloquial than то ли…, то ли….
RU-B2-05-018.tr: He said it either as a joke or in earnest – it was hard to tell.

RU-B2-05-019.notes: чтобы не + infinitive means 'so as not to': чтобы не проспать. The infinitive is usually perfective.

RU-B2-06-001.notes: же after a pronoun adds reproach: Я же тебе говорил! It assumes the listener should have known. Without же, the sentence is just a neutral statement.

RU-B2-06-002.notes: ведь appeals to something the listener already knows: you know it all, after all. It usually comes early in the clause.
RU-B2-06-002.tr: Don't worry – you know all this, after all.

RU-B2-06-003.notes: Именно (exactly, precisely) highlights the next word. It's often paired with и later in the sentence: именно это я и хотел.

RU-B2-06-004.notes: даже (even) precedes the word it highlights: даже дети. Moving it changes the meaning. In negative sentences, даже is often paired with не: даже не позвонил.

RU-B2-06-005.notes: же after a question word expresses impatience: Где же…? It's like English 'on earth'. Without же, Где мои ключи? is a neutral question.

RU-B2-07-001.notes: за + accusative gives the time taken to complete something, with a perfective verb; the plain accusative gives the duration of an activity, with an imperfective.

RU-B2-07-002.notes: The time before an event is за + accusative, and the event itself takes до + genitive: за неделю до отъезда. отъезд (departure) is a masculine noun.

RU-B2-07-003.notes: The genitive of a mass noun means 'some': купи хлеба. The accusative хлеб would mean 'the bread' or bread in general.

RU-B2-07-004.notes: Some masculine nouns have a partitive genitive in -у: чаю, сахару. It's colloquial; чая is also correct.

RU-B2-07-005.notes: The genitive of вода means 'some water': дай мне воды. The accusative воду would mean 'the water'. The same partitive genitive is used with налить, купить, выпить.

RU-B2-07-006.notes: Set phrases with не keep the genitive object: не обратил внимания. The positive is обратить внимание (accusative).

RU-B2-07-007.notes: никакой + не usually triggers the genitive: никаких писем. Total negation strongly favours the genitive.

RU-B2-07-008.notes: With не, a direct object can go into the genitive: не видел этого фильма. The accusative этот фильм is also common in speech, especially for specific things.

RU-B2-07-009.notes: желать takes the genitive of what is wished: успехов. The plural is idiomatic for this wish. The verb is often dropped: Успехов!

RU-B2-07-010.notes: желать + genitive: счастья. This is a typical toast or card greeting. The full form is Желаем вам счастья и здоровья!

RU-B2-07-011.notes: Желаю здоровья! is often said after a sneeze or in a toast. здоровье is neuter, so -я in the genitive.

RU-B2-07-012.notes: The instrumental can express manner: шёпотом (in a whisper). Likewise хором (in chorus), бегом (at a run).

RU-B2-07-013.notes: The instrumental can express the means of travel: поездом, самолётом. на поезде is equally common. The instrumental form is a little more bookish in modern speech.

RU-B2-07-014.notes: The instrumental of an ordinal gives order of arrival: пришёл первым. A woman would come первой. The same applies to последним: пришёл последним.

RU-B2-07-015.notes: достичь takes the genitive: успеха. Its masculine past has no -л: достиг, but достигла. Its imperfective is достигать, which also takes the genitive.

RU-B2-07-016.notes: избегать takes the genitive: ошибок. ошибка has a zero genitive plural with an inserted о. Its perfective is избежать: избежать ошибки.

RU-B2-07-017.notes: руководить takes the instrumental: отделом. Similar verbs: управлять, командовать. The noun руководитель means 'manager, supervisor'.

RU-B2-07-018.notes: болеть + instrumental means 'be ill with': болею гриппом. It's first conjugation (болею) in this sense.

RU-B2-07-019.notes: болеть за + accusative means 'support a team': болею за «Спартак». A fan is a болельщик. In this sense болеть conjugates like болеть 'be ill': болею, болеешь.

RU-B2-07-020.notes: завидовать takes the dative: завидует другу. The noun is зависть. Its perfective, позавидовать, is used for a single feeling.

RU-B2-08-001.notes: как бы ни + past form means 'however (much)': как бы ты ни старался. ни here is not negation but intensification.

RU-B2-08-002.notes: что бы ни + past form means 'whatever': что бы ты ни говорил. Note that что бы is two words here. The verb in the past form doesn't imply the past.
RU-B2-08-002.tip: что бы ни (whatever) is two words; чтобы (in order to) is one.

RU-B2-08-003.notes: где бы ни + past form means 'wherever': где бы я ни был. The past form is used whatever the time. The main clause keeps its normal tense.

RU-B2-08-004.notes: кто бы ни + past form means 'whoever': кто бы ни пришёл. The verb is masculine by default. The main clause is often an imperative.

RU-B2-08-005.notes: хотя бы means 'at least': хотя бы раз в неделю. It sets a minimum. It can also mean 'if only': хотя бы он позвонил!

RU-B2-08-006.notes: Пусть + third person gives 'let him / her / them': пусть он решает. Пускай is a colloquial variant. The verb follows in the present or perfective future.

RU-B2-08-007.notes: Пусть будет так is a set phrase: so be it. Пусть can also introduce a wish: пусть всё будет хорошо. The verb будет is used even though the meaning is wishful.

RU-B2-09-001.notes: прав (right) has only short forms: прав, права, правы. The cue tells you the listener is a woman: права́, with stress on the ending.

RU-B2-09-002.notes: готов (ready) is a short adjective: готов, готова, готовы. It's followed by к + dative or an infinitive.

RU-B2-09-003.notes: похож на + accusative means 'look like': похож на отца. The short form agrees with the subject. The long form, похожий, is used before a noun: похожий человек.

RU-B2-09-004.notes: согласен (agree) is a short adjective: согласен, согласна, согласны. It takes с + instrumental. A man says согласен, a group согласны.

RU-B2-09-005.notes: знаком (acquainted) is a short adjective: мы знакомы. знаком с + instrumental. The long form, знакомый, means 'acquaintance' as a noun.

RU-B2-09-006.notes: доволен (pleased) takes the instrumental: доволен результатом. The long form довольный is also used.

RU-B2-09-007.notes: Short forms of size adjectives mean 'too big / small' for someone: велико (n.), with the dative. The long form is большой.

RU-B2-09-008.notes: мал (too small) is the short form of маленький: мал, мала, мало, малы. ботинки is plural. The neuter мало also means 'little, not much'.

RU-B2-09-009.notes: The short form болен describes a temporary state (has flu); the long form больной describes a permanent quality (a sickly person).

RU-B2-09-010.notes: полон takes the genitive: полон людей. The long form полный is used before a noun. The feminine is полна, the plural полны.

RU-B2-09-011.notes: способен на + accusative means 'capable of': способен на всё. With an infinitive: способен понять. The noun is способность (ability).

RU-B2-09-012.notes: должен был + infinitive means 'should have, was supposed to': должен был позвонить. It implies it didn't happen.

RU-B2-09-013.notes: должно быть is a parenthetical meaning 'probably, must be'. It's set off by commas. It's not the same as должен, which expresses obligation.

RU-B2-09-014.notes: Possessive adjectives in -ин are formed from nouns in -а: мама → мамин. They agree like short adjectives: мамина сумка.

RU-B2-09-015.notes: Possessive adjectives in -ин decline like adjectives in the oblique cases: в маминой комнате. They're colloquial.

RU-B2-09-016.notes: по- + comparative means 'a bit more': подешевле. It's used in shops and requests. The same prefix gives побольше, поменьше, поскорее.

RU-B2-09-017.notes: по- + comparative softens a request: погромче (a bit louder). Without по- it would sound more demanding.

RU-B2-09-018.notes: самый can mean 'the very': в самом начале. It declines with the noun. самый also forms the superlative with adjectives: самый лучший.

RU-B2-09-019.notes: сам (himself) declines: самого директора (accusative animate). The stress is on the ending. The feminine is саму or самоё (bookish).

RU-B2-09-020.notes: как можно + comparative means 'as … as possible': как можно скорее. It's very common in requests. In writing, как можно раньше is also used.

RU-B2-09-021.notes: гораздо (much) strengthens a comparative: гораздо теплее. намного is a synonym. гораздо cannot be used with a positive adjective.

RU-B2-09-022.notes: всё + comparative means 'more and more': всё холоднее. It's used with verbs of change. The verb is usually imperfective: становится.

RU-B2-09-023.notes: The suffix -ейший forms a bookish superlative meaning 'most, extremely': интереснейший. It agrees like an adjective.

RU-B2-09-024.notes: одна из + genitive plural: одна из важнейших проблем. Stems in г, к, х change and take -айший instead: высокий → высочайший, строгий → строжайший.

RU-B2-10-001.notes: себя (oneself) has no nominative and refers back to the subject: думает о себе. It's the same for all persons.

RU-B2-10-002.notes: Возьми с собой means 'take with you'. собой is the instrumental of себя. Its ending -ою is archaic: с собою.

RU-B2-10-003.notes: The dative себе marks the beneficiary: купил себе. It refers back to the subject я. Without себе, the sentence would still make sense but lose the 'for myself'.
RU-B2-10-003.text: (A man speaking) Я купил {{c1::себе::себя · dative}} билет на концерт.
RU-B2-10-003.tr: I bought myself a ticket to the concert.
RU-B2-10-003.flag: dup: replaced Я купил себе новую машину (near-identical to A1 Я купил новую машину)

RU-B2-10-004.notes: чувствовать себя means 'feel' (health or mood): Как вы себя чувствуете? The reflexive pronoun is in the accusative.

RU-B2-10-005.notes: тот, кто means 'the one who, whoever'. тот takes the case of the main clause; кто that of the relative clause.
RU-B2-10-005.tr: Whoever gets up early gets a lot done.
RU-B2-10-005.flag: tr: replaced proverb (The early bird catches the worm) with a literal translation, as the Russian isn't a proverb

RU-B2-10-006.notes: A preposition can't govern a clause directly, so Russian adds то in the right case: о том, что. English needs no equivalent.

RU-B2-10-007.notes: привыкнуть к + dative: к тому, что. The demonstrative carries the case, and что introduces the clause.

RU-B2-10-008.notes: согласен с + instrumental: с тем, что. тем is the instrumental of то. The same pattern gives с тем, чтобы (in order to).

RU-B2-10-009.notes: те, кто means 'those who'. The verb in the relative clause is usually singular (кто хочет), the main verb plural.

RU-B2-10-010.notes: кое- refers to something specific that the speaker knows but doesn't name: кое-что (something). It's more definite than что-то.

RU-B2-10-011.notes: -либо means 'any at all' and is formal: какие-либо вопросы. In speech, -нибудь is used instead. -либо is typical of official forms and instructions.

RU-B2-11-001.notes: With animate nouns, два takes the accusative двух (like the genitive): двух братьев. With inanimate nouns it stays два.

RU-B2-11-002.notes: оба has the genitive обоих for masculine nouns. The noun takes the genitive plural: обоих братьев. The feminine form is обеих: у обеих сестёр.

RU-B2-11-003.notes: обе has the instrumental обеими for feminine nouns. сёстры has the instrumental сёстрами. The masculine form is обоими: с обоими братьями.

RU-B2-11-004.notes: процент takes the genitive plural after пять: процентов. на + accusative gives the amount of change.

RU-B2-11-005.notes: около + genitive: миллиона. The following noun stays genitive plural: миллиона человек. миллион declines like a masculine noun: миллиона, миллионов.
RU-B2-11-005.tr: A city with a population of about a million.

RU-B2-11-006.notes: полчаса has the genitive получаса: в течение получаса. пол- becomes полу- in the oblique cases. The same goes for полдня → полудня and полгода → полугода.

RU-B2-11-007.notes: полгода (half a year) is used in the accusative of duration. It means six months. Its genitive is полугода: больше полугода.

RU-B2-11-008.notes: Female surnames in -ова decline like adjectives in the oblique cases: с Ивановой. The male surname is Иванов.
RU-B2-11-008.text: (A man speaking) Я давно знаком с {{c1::Ивановой::Иванова · instrumental}}.
RU-B2-11-008.tr: I've known Ivanova for a long time.
RU-B2-11-008.flag: dup: replaced Я работаю с Ивановой (near-identical to A2 Я работаю с учёным)

RU-B2-11-009.notes: Plural surnames in -ов take the adjective ending -ых in the genitive: у Петровых. The whole family is meant.
RU-B2-11-009.tr: We had dinner at the Petrovs' yesterday.
RU-B2-11-009.flag: dup: replaced Мы были в гостях у Петровых (near-identical to A2 Мы были у них в гостях)

RU-B2-11-010.notes: Foreign male surnames ending in a consonant decline: Джона Смита. Foreign female surnames don't: Мэри Смит.
